Unlike the penicillins and aminoglycosides they are usual- ly bacteriostatic at the concentrations achieved in the body but act similarly to the aminoglycosides by interfering with protein synthesis in susceptible organisms. Tetracyclines all have a broad spectrum of activity which includes Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, chlamydias and chlamydophilas, rickettsias, mycoplas- mas, spirochaetes, some mycobacteria, and some proto- zoa, but the emergence of resistant strains and the develop- ment of other antimicrobials has often reduced their value. Adverse effects have also restricted their usefulness.
